lapita-culture.name: Lapita culture
lapita-culture.summary: A Neolithic Austronesian people who settled Island Melanesia by sea around 1600 to 500 BCE, known for distinctive stamped pottery and ancestral to Polynesian, Micronesian and Melanesian peoples.

austronesian-peoples.name: Austronesian peoples
austronesian-peoples.summary: Peoples descended from a prehistoric seaborne migration out of Taiwan around 3000–1500 BCE, who used sails and outrigger boats to spread across the Indo-Pacific, from Madagascar to Easter Island and New Zealand.

northern-mariana-islands.name: Northern Mariana Islands
northern-mariana-islands.summary: U.S. commonwealth made up of the 14 northern islands of the Mariana Archipelago in the Pacific; ruled successively by Spain, Germany and Japan before joining the United States as a territory in 1986.

near-oceania-and-remote-oceania.name: Remote Oceania
near-oceania-and-remote-oceania.summary: The more widely scattered parts of Oceania, including the rest of Melanesia beyond New Guinea plus Polynesia and Micronesia, distinguished from the closer islands of Near Oceania.

chamorro-people.name: Chamorro people
chamorro-people.summary: The Indigenous people of the Mariana Islands, today divided between Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands, with tens of thousands more living across the United States.

bismarck-archipelago.name: Bismarck Archipelago
bismarck-archipelago.summary: A group of islands off the northeastern coast of New Guinea, part of Papua New Guinea, covering about 50,000 square kilometres.

artocarpus-camansi.name: Artocarpus camansi (breadnut)
artocarpus-camansi.summary: A tree native to New Guinea and nearby islands whose seeded fruit is the wild ancestor of the modern breadfruit.

catamaran.name: Double-hulled canoe
catamaran.summary: A vessel with two hulls lashed together, invented by Austronesian peoples and used for long voyages across the Indian and Pacific Oceans.

mariana-islands.name: Mariana Islands
mariana-islands.summary: A crescent-shaped Pacific archipelago north of New Guinea, home to the indigenous Chamorro people, now divided between the US Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands and the territory of Guam.

lashed-lug-boat.name: Lashed-lug boat
lashed-lug-boat.summary: An ancient Austronesian boat-building technique using lugs carved into hull planks, lashed together with fiber rope instead of metal fastenings.

austronesian-sail-types.name: Crab claw sail
austronesian-sail-types.summary: A triangular Austronesian sail with spars along its upper and lower edges, developed by at least 2000 BCE and used together with catamarans and outrigger boats.

admiralty-islands.name: Admiralty Islands
admiralty-islands.summary: An archipelago of 40 rainforest-covered islands in the Bismarck Archipelago north of New Guinea, also called the Manus Islands, forming Papua New Guinea's Manus Province.

luzon.name: Luzon
luzon.summary: Largest and most populous island of the Philippines, home to the capital Manila and Quezon City. It holds more than half the country's population.

edward-winslow-gifford.name: Edward Winslow Gifford
edward-winslow-gifford.summary: American anthropologist (1887-1959) who devoted his life to studying California Indian ethnography. He was a professor and director of the Museum of Anthropology at the University of California, Berkeley.

radiocarbon-dating.name: Radiocarbon dating
radiocarbon-dating.summary: Method for finding the age of organic material by measuring its radioactive carbon-14, which decays after death. Developed in the late 1940s by Willard Libby, it reliably dates objects up to about 50,000 years old.

melanesians.name: Melanesians
melanesians.summary: Predominant Indigenous inhabitants of Melanesia, an area stretching from New Guinea to the Fiji Islands. Most speak Austronesian or Papuan languages.

austronesian-languages.name: Austronesian languages
austronesian-languages.summary: A family of roughly 1,257 languages spoken by about 386 million people across Maritime Southeast Asia, Madagascar, Taiwan and the Pacific, including Malay, Javanese and Tagalog.
